correctness.rationale: The complete corrected RESULT.md under repairs/4 gives the formulas for fixed d≥3. The coprime generators a and da+b ensure cofiniteness and the least positive generator is a. Vandermonde bounds the total represented binomial value by the binomial at the total index cost, proving the lower bound c_d n^(1/d). To check the upper bound independently, if k is the largest admissible index, the bounds for the binomial product put c_d n^(1/d) in [k−d+1,k+1). Pascal's identity bounds the remainder r by O_d((n+1)^((d−1)/d)), with r<n. Since (r+1)^(1/d)/(n+1)^(1/d)≤1/2 for all sufficiently large n, strong induction first gives a global bound A_d(n+1)^(1/d) (cover bounded n by the unit coin). Applying that bound only to the first remainder gives O_d((n+1)^η_d), including n=0. In residue br the binomial value has form r+ja with j≥0, by coprimality and nonnegativity; index below d only adds multiples of a. The least residue element is br+a times the index-cost envelope above br, i.e. w_r=br+a min_j(μ_d(r+ja)+bj). Every j gives the same required lower bound and j=0 gives the upper bound uniformly in b, whether or not it minimizes. Counting individual residue gaps gives the Apéry max-minus-a and sum identities. Taking r=a−1 for the lower maximum and bounding monotonically for the upper, and using integral comparison for the genus sum, gives both constants and O_d(a^(1+η_d)); all estimates include a≥2 and the residue r=0. The frozen script was inspected (it tests finite residue minima), not executed.

evidence: For f(n)=(1+√(8n+1))/2, the quadratic cost is between f(n) and f(n)+3f((f(n)−2)/3) at positive n. Hence it is √(2n)+O((n+1)^(1/4)). Outside eight fixed exceptions, Theorem 8.1 takes the maximum of aμ_2(r)+br minus a for F and the sum of μ_2(r) plus (a−1)(b−1)/2 for genus.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Evaluating the lower maximum at a−1 and taking a monotone upper envelope gives coefficient √2 and O(a^(5/4)); summing the cost and using an integral gives 2√2/3 and the same error. The fixed exceptions are absorbed, and the constants do not depend on b. Thus the degree-two refinement is already implied even though §8 explicitly reports only weaker asymptotic bounds. For d≥3 that inference has no corresponding prior cost estimate in the material inspected; the lower/upper binomial index bound and envelope allow unrestricted b without identifying the exact minimizing lift.
